emy|five.note: UNRULED. The forms are written in MODERN Mayan orthography (utz, jun) rather than in a Classic-period transliteration, which is the shape a comparative wordlist has, not an epigraphic one. Two Mayan priors have already been wrong in this atlas, so these want a check against a hieroglyphic lexicon (Boot, Kettunen & Helmke) rather than a ruling from the shape.

omx|eye.note: UNRULED, and the likeliest remaining leak. Old Mon has NO wordEvidence at all and the row comment says "Reconstructions follow Shorto (1971) and Diffloth" — the word "reconstructions" on a language attested in dated inscriptions. Shorto's Dictionary of the Mon Inscriptions should give the inscriptional form directly.

omx|water.note: UNRULED, and the clearest tell in the group: the IPA writes the implosive ɗaːk, which is Proto-Austroasiatic house notation. Old Mon orthography is ḍāk / dāk. An implosive in an attested language's IPA, matching the proto row byte for byte, is what a copied reconstruction looks like.

pyx|star.note: leak, known and accepted for now. Declared evidence: inferred, source Tibeto-Burman comparative (*s-kar) — the cell says what it is, which is why review 546 left it standing while emptying the eleven that claimed direct attestation. kar· does occur twice in the corpus (inscription 027) but no source glosses it. pyx|you.note: leak, known and accepted for now. Declared evidence: inferred, source Tibeto-Burman comparative (*naŋ). naṅ· occurs once (inscription 178), unglossed. Same open policy question as pyx|star. Note obr|you holds the identical form and IS attested.

zkt|good.note: UNRULED, and genuinely doubtful. Khitan is only PARTIALLY deciphered — the large script especially — so a Khitan cell agreeing byte for byte with Proto-Mongolic is not obviously inheritance. sajin/sain and bi are Mongolic shapes, which is exactly what someone reaching for the proto row would produce. Needs a reading from the Khitan epigraphic literature (Kane, Wu & Janhunen) per cell.
